title: Resurrexit
readingOutcome: Read completed past actions in Creed and Gospel narrative.

authoringPolicy.method: short concept introduction → authentic example → guided recognition → controlled manipulation → liturgical reading → retrieval
authoringPolicy.vocabularyPolicy: Frozen Lesson 15 vocabulary only; narrative support vocabulary is declared explicitly.
authoringPolicy.authenticTextPolicy: Perfect forms are read in Creed and Gospel narrative clauses rather than synthetic prose.
authoringPolicy.copyrightPolicy: Pedagogical prose and exercises are original synthesis.

sources.sourceLatin: Et resurrexit tertia die, secundum Scripturas. Et ascendit in caelum: sedet ad dexteram Patris.
sources.provenanceNote: resurrexit and ascendit are completed actions; sedet contrasts with present state.

sources.sourceLatin: Surrexit, non est hic: ecce locus ubi posuerunt eum.
sources.provenanceNote: Surrexit gives a compact perfect narrative anchor; later clause material is mostly recycled or supplied.

sources.sourceLatin: Et invenerunt lapidem revolutum a monumento.
sources.provenanceNote: invenerunt gives third-person plural perfect in Easter narrative.

sources.sourceLatin: Qui propter nos homines et propter nostram salutem descendit de caelis.
sources.provenanceNote: descendit is read as the completed Creed action 'came down'.

sources.sourceLatin: Et accesserunt, et tenuerunt pedes ejus, et adoraverunt eum.
sources.provenanceNote: accesserunt introduces perfect accedo and recycles ejus/eum pronoun forms.

sources.sourceLatin: Ceciderunt in faciem suam, et timuerunt valde.
sources.provenanceNote: ceciderunt is perfect of cado and reuses facies/suus; timuerunt is left as supplied support by meaning.
ago is introduced through the fixed liturgical phrase gratias agamus.

casePanel.policy: All six cases remain active. Narrative tense recognition now operates alongside case, pronoun and preposition reading.

perfectFramework.caution: Perfect stems can change substantially: resurgo → resurrexit, surgo → surrexit, invenio → invenerunt, cado → ceciderunt.
perfectFramework.readingValue: completed event or action viewed as a whole

pronounSpiral.focus: Resolve third-person pronoun forms inside completed Gospel actions.
pronounSpiral.rule: Use case and antecedent/context together; do not translate a pronoun in isolation.

learnerCopy.en: The perfect presents an event as completed or viewed as a whole. This makes it central to Creed and Gospel narrative: He rose, ascended, came down; they found, approached, fell.
learnerCopy.fr: Le parfait présente un événement comme accompli ou envisagé dans son ensemble. Il est donc central dans le Credo et le récit évangélique : il ressuscita, monta, descendit ; ils trouvèrent, s'approchèrent, tombèrent.

learnerCopy.en: A common perfect active family is -i, -isti, -it, -imus, -istis, -erunt. But the stem often changes, so recognition must combine ending and lemma: resurrexit belongs to resurgo; ceciderunt belongs to cado.
learnerCopy.fr: Une famille fréquente de terminaisons du parfait actif est -i, -isti, -it, -imus, -istis, -erunt. Mais le radical change souvent : resurrexit appartient à resurgo ; ceciderunt à cado.

learnerCopy.en: The Creed puts two completed actions beside a present state: resurrexit, ascendit, then sedet. Tense contrast helps the reader see the sequence rather than merely decode endings.
learnerCopy.fr: Le Credo place deux actions accomplies à côté d'un état présent : resurrexit, ascendit, puis sedet. Le contraste des temps aide à voir la séquence, au-delà des seules terminaisons.

learnerCopy.en: surgo and resurgo are distinct lemmas. Surrexit means 'he rose'; resurrexit means 'he rose again'. Do not collapse them because their perfect forms look related.
learnerCopy.fr: surgo et resurgo sont deux lemmes distincts. Surrexit signifie « il se leva » ; resurrexit « il ressuscita / se releva de nouveau ». Il ne faut pas les confondre.

learnerCopy.en: ejus is genitive singular of is/ea/id; eum is accusative masculine singular. The perfect verbs tell what happened; the pronouns tell whose feet and whom they adored.
learnerCopy.fr: ejus est le génitif singulier de is/ea/id ; eum l'accusatif masculin singulier. Les verbes au parfait disent ce qui s'est passé ; les pronoms indiquent à qui appartiennent les pieds et qui fut adoré.

learningBlocks.title: Stage 3: from tense drills to narrative

learnerCopy.en: The Stage 3 gate asks you to read short Psalm/Gospel narrative clauses by combining tense, case, pronoun and connector recognition. The milestone is not full translation without support; it is reliable structural reading of authentic narrative.
learnerCopy.fr: Le contrôle de l'étape 3 demande de lire de courtes propositions narratives de psaume ou d'Évangile en combinant temps, cas, pronoms et connecteurs. L'objectif n'est pas encore une traduction totalement autonome, mais une lecture structurelle fiable du récit authentique.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Et resurrexit tertia die, secundum Scripturas. Et ascendit in caelum: sedet ad dexteram Patris.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Et resurrexit tertia die, secundum Scripturas. Et ascendit in caelum: sedet ad dexteram Patris.

translation.en: And He rose again the third day according to the Scriptures. And He ascended into heaven: He sitteth at the right hand of the Father.
translation.fr: Et il ressuscita le troisième jour, conformément aux Écritures. Et il monta au ciel : il siège à la droite du Père.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Surrexit, non est hic: ecce locus ubi posuerunt eum.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Surrexit, non est hic: ecce locus ubi posuerunt eum.

translation.en: He is risen; He is not here: behold the place where they laid Him.
translation.fr: Il est ressuscité ; il n'est pas ici : voici le lieu où ils l'ont déposé.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Et invenerunt lapidem revolutum a monumento.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Et invenerunt lapidem revolutum a monumento.

translation.en: And they found the stone rolled back from the tomb.
translation.fr: Et elles trouvèrent la pierre roulée loin du tombeau.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Qui propter nos homines et propter nostram salutem descendit de caelis.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Qui propter nos homines et propter nostram salutem descendit de caelis.

translation.en: Who for us men and for our salvation came down from heaven.
translation.fr: Qui, pour nous les hommes et pour notre salut, descendit des cieux.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Et accesserunt, et tenuerunt pedes ejus, et adoraverunt eum.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Et accesserunt, et tenuerunt pedes ejus, et adoraverunt eum.

translation.en: And they came up, and took hold of His feet, and adored Him.
translation.fr: Elles s'approchèrent, saisirent ses pieds et l'adorèrent.

authenticPassages.sourceLatin: Ceciderunt in faciem suam, et timuerunt valde.
authenticPassages.instructionalDisplay: Ceciderunt in faciem suam, et timuerunt valde.

translation.en: They fell upon their face, and were very much afraid.
translation.fr: Ils tombèrent face contre terre et eurent une grande crainte.

translation.en: Let us give thanks to the Lord our God.
translation.fr: Rendons grâce au Seigneur notre Dieu.

exercises.hint: It presents a completed Creed event.
exercises.explanation: resurrexit is perfect active of resurgo.

exercises.prompt: Which verb remains present in the Credo sequence?
exercises.hint: Two are completed events; one is a current state.
exercises.explanation: sedet is present while resurrexit and ascendit are perfect.

exercises.hint: Do not confuse surgo with resurgo.
The -erunt ending is a strong perfect clue.

exercises.prompt: What pronoun family does ejus belong to?
exercises.explanation: ejus is genitive singular of is/ea/id.

exercises.prompt: What case is eum in adoraverunt eum?
exercises.hint: It is the object of adoraverunt.

exercises.prompt: Which perfect form comes from cado?
exercises.explanation: ceciderunt is perfect plural of cado.
Stage 3 is a tense system, not three isolated chapters.

exercises.stimulus: Et accesserunt, et tenuerunt pedes ejus, et adoraverunt eum.
exercises.explanation: The clause is a chain of perfect actions.

exercises.prompt: What case is faciem in in faciem suam?
exercises.hint: Here in expresses motion/result toward a position.
exercises.explanation: faciem is accusative after directional in.

exercises.hint: This is the frozen Lesson 15 target.
exercises.explanation: Stage 3 ends at short narrative-clause reading.

exercises.prompt: Which lesson intentionally continues the pronoun spiral here?
exercises.hint: The curriculum requires repeated pronoun retrieval.
exercises.explanation: Lesson 15 reuses third-person pronouns inside narrative.

objectives: Recognize perfect active as completed event.
Distinguish surgo/resurgo and strong perfect stems.
Continue the pronoun spiral through ejus/eum.
Pass the Stage 3 Psalm/Gospel narrative checkpoint.
